title: NETFLOW: Add decodes for Juniper Networks proprietary IE's
description:
Modified the Netflow dissector to decode Juniper Proprietary IE's
and decode IE 315 (data link frame section).

notes.body: ti is not used ?
yes you are right the ti in line 7991 is not used as apposed to the ti in line 7995. Will remove that.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2585/diffs?diff_id=168713840&start_sha=13fe355473c7d2fe4b848914b85e5d268bb0c565#5eb10f20ad0e037a4b8467ec945fa5097b06e701_7991_7995)
Not realy useful with on entry in the value string.
I am guessing you mean Ok to hav as a value_string, but doing the _ext lookup for only one known value?

Yes

Den lör 3 apr. 2021 17:17Martin Mathieson (@martin.r.mathieson) <
gitlab@mg.gitlab.com> skrev:
Well there is a val_to_str functon to use too. But no big deal.

We can use val_to_str() but the since the code already uses val_to_str_ext() to print info regarding propreitary IE's of other Enterprises. I don't suppose i can change the call to that API as other enterprises have already implemented the code keeping the API val_to_str_ext() in mind.
I would move this further up, maybe around line 159?
Sure will do that

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2585/diffs?diff_id=168713840&start_sha=13fe355473c7d2fe4b848914b85e5d268bb0c565#5eb10f20ad0e037a4b8467ec945fa5097b06e701_3641_3642)
Can we have a comment to say why we are storing/restoring addresses?  Would it display wrong, or not find the right conversation?

Sure will add a comment.
The storing and restoring of the addresses is required because when we pass the remaining packet to the eth dissector it will change the info table and replace the source and destination address of the Netflow packet with the addresses of the packet carried by IE 315. That would be wrong as the actual source and destination of the packet are not those which are seen in l2 packet of IE315 but those represented by the Netflow IP header.
One more leading space wanted here.
sure.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2585/diffs?diff_id=168713840&start_sha=13fe355473c7d2fe4b848914b85e5d268bb0c565#5eb10f20ad0e037a4b8467ec945fa5097b06e701_7986_7995)
What is length is neither 2 nor 4?  Is this possible?  Do we need to flag other values with expert info?
The IE only supports length 2 and 4. It is not possible to have any other length other than 2 and 4.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2585/diffs?diff_id=168713840&start_sha=13fe355473c7d2fe4b848914b85e5d268bb0c565#5eb10f20ad0e037a4b8467ec945fa5097b06e701_8005_7995)
*If* it was possible for length to be neither 2 nor 4, then the value of cpid would be undefined here..?  Surprised there is no compiler warning, but I might well be missing something.
As stated above there can be only 2 conditions of length 2 and 4 . We don't expect any other value. So it will always hit the if else block and cpid will have a value.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2585/diffs?diff_id=168713840&start_sha=13fe355473c7d2fe4b848914b85e5d268bb0c565#5eb10f20ad0e037a4b8467ec945fa5097b06e701_8006_7995)
So it couldn't be, even in a malformed of fuzzed frame?
yes
